subject: Sapphire-3b latency spike — proposed traffic quarantine & SLA carveout
messages:
From: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@crestbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T07:12:00-08:00
Subject: Spike in p95 on sapphire-3b since 11/16 — urgent

Kim,

We started seeing elevated p95 latency for calls routed to model 'sapphire-3b' over the last 48 hours. Our telemetry shows a sustained p95 increase from ~280ms to ~1.1s during peak windows (08:00–10:00 PT). Errors are low, but request timeouts for some downstream services are being triggered. This is violating our SLA target of p95 < 500ms for the 'sapphire-3b' route.

We've attached a short latency report (crestbank_sapphire3b_latency_1116-1118.pdf) with the raw percentiles and a sample trace. Can your team either pin us to the previous stable variant or quarantine traffic to a fallback while you investigate? We need a temporary mitigation plan and approval path for an SLA exception if the change is going to take time.

Liam
Liam O'Neil
Senior SRE, CrestBank
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@crestbank.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T07:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Spike in p95 on sapphire-3b since 11/16 — urgent

Thanks for the report, Liam — and looping in Ben and Neha to confirm next steps. High level: we need a short-lived mitigation that preserves quality where possible and a formal SLA carveout if we activate any traffic quarantine that increases customer p95 beyond their committed threshold.

Ben/Eng: please advise whether we can immediately: 1) pin CrestBank to sapphire-3b@v20261110 (previous stable), or 2) route up to 40% of their traffic to sapphire-3b-safe (quantized variant) and enable a quarantine route while you triage. Include estimated delta on quality (BLEU/ROUGE or internal eval) and expected time to restore.

Neha/Finance: if we grant CrestBank a provisional SLA exception (72 hours) during remediation, what billing/credit implications do we need to document?

Marissa/CS: please prep a short customer-facing note if we need to declare an exception and include the temporary mitigation plan.

Urgency: please respond in the next 2 hours so I can reply with an interim plan to the customer and request formal carveout approval.

Thanks — Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@crestbank.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Spike in p95 on sapphire-3b since 11/16 — urgent

Quick technical readout: we've pulled runtime telemetry and two things stand out — a kernel scheduling change rolled to a subset of serving nodes on 11/15 that increases tail latency for models with longer attention windows, and a heavier tokenization distribution spike from CrestBank's payloads that exacerbates the effect.

Options and recommended immediate action:
- Pin traffic: we can pin CrestBank to sapphire-3b@v20261110 immediately; downside is reduced ability to receive security/bugfix patches. Rollback takes ~10 minutes to route config change and an additional ~30 for cache warmup.
- Quarantine & split: create a routing policy (route:quarantine-sapphire-3b) that routes 60% to stable v20261110 and 40% to sapphire-3b-safe (quantized) until we have a hotfix. Expected p95 for the split: ~420–600ms (best-case) but sapphire-3b-safe shows minor quality regressions on long-context prompts (~1–2% metric delta).
- Hotfix: engineering can roll a targeted kernel patch to affected nodes; ETA 8–12 hours with high confidence.

I recommend quarantine & split as an immediate mitigation to reduce SLA exposure while we build/verify the hotfix. I've attached the routing policy diff (routing_policy_quarantine.diff) that implements the policy and TTL for the quarantined cache keys.

If we proceed with the split, we should also request a provisional SLA carveout (72 hours) for CrestBank to avoid automatic SLA credits while hotfix is applied.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@crestbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Spike in p95 on sapphire-3b since 11/16 — urgent

Liam — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the report. Interim plan below (effective immediately once we get your acknowledgement):

1) Traffic quarantine: we'll enable route:quarantine-sapphire-3b and split CrestBank traffic 60% -> sapphire-3b@v20261110 (stable) / 40% -> sapphire-3b-safe (quantized fallback). Expect visible p95 improvement within the first 20 minutes of the routing change; quality delta on long-context prompts should be small but CS will validate.

2) Hotfix effort: Engineering will start a targeted kernel fix now; ETA 8–12 hours. We will keep you updated on build/test progress and expected completion time.

3) SLA carveout request: we are requesting a provisional 72-hour SLA exception window for CrestBank to cover the mitigation window (so that automated SLA credits are not triggered). If the hotfix completes earlier we will rescind immediately.

Please reply with a short OK to proceed for the quarantine+carveout. If you prefer immediate pin to v20261110 instead of the split, say so and we will implement the pin.

Marissa will follow up with the formal customer note and the CS playbook for verification. Neha, please confirm billing/credit language to include in the customer notice.

Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
